summary: The changed application itself was run and captured. context/hosted-preview.json records a real maintainer-verified static-preview-v1 deployment (project deos-preview-554b6e57d5a22469, deployment 5d8ffabe..., status success, all assets HTTP 200), and every published asset sha256 (app.js ddff27f6, domain.js ed6502b8, storage.js 4ddc3ff5, index.html c8a44f88, styles.css 275efad5, review-harness.js 02db56ba) equals the reviewed candidate file hash in the manifest, so the screenshots exercise exactly the reviewed code rather than a fixture page. All fifteen images render the real application at 1440x900 and show app-generated state, not mock-ups: live status text ("Expense saved.", "Expense updated.", "Expense saved. The filter changed to All so the new expense is visible.", "Expenses changed in another tab. Review the latest list, then retry your change."), the code's exact validation strings ("Enter a name.", "Amount can have no more than two decimal places.", "Amount must be more than zero.", "Choose Food, Travel, Bills, or Other."), aria-pressed filter styling, and BigInt-derived euro totals that match the rows. I inspected the harness: review-harness.js only writes the app's own expense-tracker:v1 key with valid seed documents (guarded by sessionStorage so a reload does not re-seed), injects one clearly banner-labeled "Entertainment" option, and offers one another-tab write. It never fakes rendered rows, totals, receipts, or messages, and it contains no delete/edit/add path, so each mutation shown had to run through the application's own validate -> preflight -> write -> commit flow. Because the seed is written once per session, the post-refresh captures (Power bill alone at €45.75 after a delete, and Lunch €15.00 + Coffee €3.00 = €18.00 after the recovery/retry sequence) are genuine proof that the app persisted its own writes to browser storage across a real reload, not re-seeded fixtures. All nine approved requirements are covered: add, edit of all three fields, delete, the three approved validation rejections with unchanged saved values, Food/Bills/All filtering with €12.50/€0.00/€32.50 visible totals, refresh persistence with no resurrected deletion, single anonymous desktop screen with no login or outside service, and the human-required harness-labeled allowlist probe. Human decisions in context/issue-and-feedback.json are respected: publication used static-preview-v1 only (no CI, account setup, or production release), the change stops at an unmerged implementation PR, the forced invalid-category probe is visibly labeled both in the page banner and the caption, and Claude chose the demonstration count. Residual, non-blocking observations for the PR reviewer: the plan promised Showboat "operation: measure" records of live origin/viewport/text, and the single Showboat item is instead a node behavior-proof script (origin and asset integrity are independently established by the trusted hosted-preview record); several planned intermediate checkpoints were not captured (the €12.50 state after the first add, the open edit editor pre-save, the moment of deletion before refresh, the successful 1.99 retry, and the post-clear empty state), though each of those outcomes is visible as carried-forward state in a later capture (for example Snack €1.99 with total €14.49 appears in the rejected-zero-edit image). These are evidence-density gaps inside otherwise demonstrated scenarios, not missing behavior.
